# Priced implementation and instruction bounds

All counts are executed scalar AArch64 instructions (64-bit general registers; arithmetic, logic, loads,
stores, address formation, branches, calls and returns count one each). They are counts of supplied or
generated listings, not timings. One processor; W = R/20,000.

## Evidence chain

* Step loop: generated by `walks.py` part S (digit tag and 6-adding configuration of submission
  70974bf7, unrolled as in f86cff50), encoding-validated and executed trip by trip against the definition
  (144 per certified trip, both trips). The base package's `ttstep.c` / `ttstep.disasm.txt` (128-bit-word
  tag, 273 per trip, recounted by its `experiment.py`) remain the reference implementation of the base method.
* Digit conversion: generated by `walks.py` (`build_digits2`), 171 straight-line instructions, executed by
  part I on every re-base and by part T, with its digits compared with the definition.
* Exact evaluation: generated by `walks.py` (`build_exact`) with part L's generator, 1,294 straight-line
  instructions, executed by part I and compared with the true t.
* Window product: generated by `lazy.py` part L as one straight-line program and executed instruction by
  instruction on a simulator of the scalar subset it uses (LDP/STP/LDR, MUL/UMULH, ADDS/ADCS/ADC,
  SUBS/SBCS/SBC, EXTR/LSL, CSEL, UDIV, ADD/SUB-immediate, ADR, RET), compared with big-integer products;
  executed length **8,679** on every input (straight line). Before execution an encoding validator checks
  every instruction: LDP/STP offsets multiples of 8 in [-512, 504], LDR/LDUR offsets encodable, ADD/SUB
  immediates 12-bit (optionally shifted by 12), shift amounts 0..63, x18 unused, SP only as a base or in
  ADD/SUB-immediate; part L reports 0 violations. `{"seed":1,"listings":true}` prints the listing.
* `fr_add` (label updates) and the remaining tower routines (setup, exact evaluation, table build):
  `tower.c` / `tower.disasm.txt` of the base package, recounted by `experiment.py`.

## The step loop: 144 instructions per step (generated, `walks.py` part S)

Registers:
- x0 = P (current entry pointer in trip A), x10 = P (trip B);
- x1 = the 72 digits of Y0, x2 = trip budget, x3 = A;
- x4 = THR6 = 2^64 - 14 x 2^48 (one MOVN per call), x17 = 6 (one MOV per call);
- x5/x6 = a pair of entry words, x7/x8 = a pair of reloaded digits, x9 = scratch;
- digits 54..71 resident in x11..x16 and x19..x30 (18 registers, loaded once per call).

One trip (trip A shown; trip B swaps x0 and x10):

1. For each pair of digits j, j+1: `ldp x5, x6, [x0, #off_j]` (two entry words); the two digits from
   resident registers or `ldp x7, x8, [x1, #8j]` (digits 0..53); `madd x3, d_j, x5, x3` and
   `madd x3, d_(j+1), x6, x3` (`mul` for the first). That is 36 LDP of words + 27 LDP of digits + 71 MADD
   + 1 MUL = 135.
2. Certificate: `mul x9, x3, x17` (L = 6A mod 2^64); `sub x9, x9, #1`; `cmp x9, x4`; `b.hs EXACT`. Certified
   iff 1 <= L <= THR6, the test of proof.md section 2.
3. Selector and child: `umulh x9, x3, x17` (s = floor(6A/2^64)); `ldr x10, [x0, x9, lsl #3]`; `cbz x10, REBASE`.
4. Budget: `subs x2, x2, #1`; `b.eq BUDGET` (trip A) or `b.ne LOOP` (trip B, the one backward branch).

That makes **144** (the digit tag and 6-adding configuration follow 70974bf7; the unrolling without a
per-trip MOV follows f86cff50). Every offset is encodable (validated): entry words 0..63 at P - 512 .. P - 8
and 64..71 at P + 48 .. P + 104, child pointers at P + 0 .. P + 40, reloaded digits at x1 + 0 .. x1 + 416.
The trips have no call and no store, and their forward exits are not taken on a certified in-window trip.
Such a trip therefore executes exactly 144 instructions; part S checks the executed length of every trip in
both trips. The prologue (frame, cursor pointer, `movn x4`, `mov x17`, 6 STP, one ADD to reach digit 54,
9 LDP of resident digits) is 20 instructions. Each exit path (an exit from trip B first copies x10 to x0;
then store the cursor, status, 6 LDP, frame, RET) is at most 13, once per call.

## Table entry

Entries are addressed by P = entry + 512. A **non-leaf** entry is 1,072 bytes:
- entry words 0..63 at P - 512 .. P - 8, the 6 child pointers (each of the same form) at P .. P + 47, and
  words 64..71 at P + 48 .. P + 111;
- then the exact row v(T_e) as 12 Montgomery residues (384 bytes) and 8 words (alpha, beta).

A **leaf** (depth 1280, null child pointers) additionally holds T_e as its 54 canonical Karatsuba operands
(1,728 bytes, in the order of `lazy.py` `table_operands`), 2,800 bytes in all.

The step loop reads only the 72 words and the pointers; the exact evaluation reads the row; the window
product reads a leaf's operands.

## Window end: at most 9,216 instructions

`rebase` = Y0 <- Y0 * T_e by the generated routine (8,679, including its frame: SUB sp by #1, LSL #12 and
by #112, saves and restores of x19..x30 at [sp, 0..80], four scratch base registers by ADD sp, #624 +
1024 i, ADR of the constant pool, and `ret`), then the generated digit conversion of the 12 output
coordinates into 72 digits (171: per coordinate 2 LDP, UBFX, EXTR + AND, EXTR + AND, UBFX, EXTR + AND,
LSR, 3 STP; two ADDs for the second windows; RET), plus two label additions mod r with the base package's
`fr_add` (34 each), plus 20 instructions of glue (call site, pointer set-up). That is 8,938.

**The generated product.** It uses the Fp12 = Fp4[t]/(t^3 - s), Fp4 = Fp2[s]/(s^2 - xi) grouping of the
stored coordinates, with cubic Karatsuba over Fp4, Karatsuba over Fp2 and Karatsuba Fp2, 54
256x256-bit products (67 instructions each: 4 LDP, 16 MUL, 16 UMULH, 31 ADDS/ADCS/ADC). Fp2- and Fp4-level results stay unreduced as 9-word
two's-complement values. Each of the 12 output coordinates is one accumulator over the Fp4-level values,
plus one constant multiple of p, and then a single Montgomery reduction with canonicalisation (107
instructions). That makes 12 reductions instead of 54 (lazy reduction, Aranha et al., eprint 2010/526).

The generator asserts worst-case bounds for every stored value: operands < 2^256, products < 2^512,
intermediates in (-2^575, 2^575), reduction input >= 0, t < 2^264 after the word rounds, and
remainder < 2p before the final conditional subtraction. The output is canonical, Y0 * T_e in Montgomery
form, which is the form the step loop reads. Opcode histogram (part L): ADCS 1,808, LDP 1,438, MUL
1,104, UMULH 1,092, SBCS 920, ADC 590, STP 558, ADDS 542, SUBS 200, EXTR 172, SBC 116, CSEL 96, LSL 20,
UDIV 12, ADD/SUB-immediate 9, ADR 1, RET 1.

One window end = re-base 8,938 + loop entry 20 + exit 13 + driver <= 160 = 9,131 <= **9,216**.

## The driver: a three-word global step counter

As in the base package, except that the global step counter (initially 2^140) is a **three-word**
integer and the per-walk length counter (initially 2^90) a two-word integer. Before each call the driver
sets the 64-bit trip budget to min(steps left, walk length left, 2^62). After the call it subtracts the
trips made from both counters (three-word and two-word subtractions with borrow, and compares). It
dispatches REBASE (window end), EXACT (uncertified tag) and BUDGET (a counter reached zero) exactly as
the base package describes. All driver work per call is below 160 instructions (base: 128 with two-word
counters). The extra word costs 4 instructions (one SBCS and one comparison step each). Every call ends
within 1280 trips, so this is charged once per window end.

**Counter widths.** Every cap is enforced by a counter wide enough to hold it, and the update cost is
inside the price stated for the item it counts:

| counter | cap | width | update | charged in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| global step counter | 2^140 | 3 words | subtract with borrow + compare, <= 8 per call | driver <= 160 per call |
| per-walk length counter | 2^90 | 2 words | subtract with borrow + compare, <= 6 per call | driver <= 160 per call |
| trip budget | 2^62 | 1 word | `subs x2, x2, #1` | the 144 of a trip |
| walk counter | 2^52 | 1 word | add + compare, 3 per walk | walk start (< 2^26) |
| exact-evaluation meter | 2^127 | 2 words | add with carry + compare, <= 4 | exact evaluation (1,792) |
| store-probe meter | 2^70 | 2 words | add with carry + compare, <= 4 | store probe (32) |

No counter can wrap.

## Exact evaluation (metered, at most 2^127 times): at most 1,792 instructions

Taken when the tag is not certified, with probability (14 2^48 + 2)/2^64 = 2^-12.19 per step under H2r
(proof.md section 6), so its price enters the expected work per step (1,792 x 2^-12.19 = 0.39). There is no
re-base: t(Y0 T_e) = sum_k y_k v_k(T_e) is computed from Y0's stored residues and the entry's row. Itemised:
- the generated routine (`walks.py` `build_exact`, executed by part I): 12 products accumulated unreduced,
  one Montgomery reduction with canonicalisation, then t~ x 1 and a second reduction, with frame, **1,294**;
- s by five four-limb comparisons with stored multiples of p/6, and the distinguished test
  t < ceil(p/2^84) by one, under 60;
- the aborted trip, under 144;
- one loop exit (13) and re-entry (20);
- the driver, at most 160;
- the meter, at most 4.

In all at most 1,294 + 60 + 144 + 13 + 20 + 160 + 4 = 1,695, **charged 1,792**.

## Fixed work, all inside F = 2^110

| item | bound |
|---|---:|
| gate: one 64-bit random word and a comparison | < 2^5 |
| parse the input, basis change, Montgomery conversion, z^r = 1 (<= 508 fp12_mul of `tower.c`) | < 2^25 |
| 16 multiplier scalars and 8 multipliers | < 2^30 |
| table: 6,209,268,427,492,417 = C(1286,6) entries; each one fp12_mul of `tower.c` (24,044), the row v(T_e) (< 2^14), 72 values u and words (< 2^11 each), the 42 operand sums (35 each with `fp_add`), labels, 8 child pointers (< 2^9 each): below 2^18 per entry, charged 2^20 | < 2^73 |
| walk starts: at most 2^52, each with rejection-sampled scalars and two exponentiations (< 2^26) | < 2^78 |
| store: at most 2^52 inserts and lookups in 2^54 slots of 96 bytes, at most 2^70 probes (meter: a two-word counter, at most 4 instructions per update, inside the 32 per probe), 32 instructions per probe | < 2^75 |
| false matches and the final hit: at most 2^52 recoveries (< 2^18) and verifications g^x = z (< 2^25) | < 2^78 |
| output Q = [x]Q0: 254 affine doublings and at most 254 additions over Fp2 with one inversion each (as in 73463878), serialization of P0 and Q | < 2^30 |
| every cap/failure path, allocation, code loading | < 2^40 |
| **sum** (exact evaluations are charged separately, above) | < 2^81 < **2^110** |

## Storage

Table: 6,209,268,427,492,417 non-leaf-sized entries x 1,072 bytes plus 28,970,148,184,257 leaves x 1,728
further bytes = 2^62.541 bytes. Store: 2^54 x 96 = 2^60.585 bytes. The digit buffer, multipliers, constants,
binomial table, code, stacks and the routines' 4 KiB frames take under 2^31 bytes. Peak below
2^62.541 + 2^60.585 + 2^31 < 2^62.88, so **below 2^63 bytes**. Every address is an ordinary 64-bit pointer
below 2^63. Memory is reported, not scored.

## Totals (`lazy.py` part G)

Per step 144 + 9,216/1280 + 1,792 x (14 2^48 + 2)/2^64 <= **151.59** instructions in expectation (window length 1280).

    every run:  R <= 144 x 2^140 + 9,216 (2^140/1280 + 2^52 + 1) + 1,792 x 2^127 + 2^110,  W <= 2^132.96
    expected:   E[R_run] <= 144 E[T] + 9,216 (E[T]/1280 + E[walks] + 1) + 1,792 E[X] + 2^110,  E[T] <= 2^127.3667
                E[W] <= 1 + (K/2^64) E[R_run]/20,000 <= 2^118.9732 <= 2^118.98
